content.user_title: Analyze Structured Data with jq and yq
content.value_statement: Structured files are hard to inspect quickly when they are large or nested. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code build focused jq and yq commands.
actual_capabilities: Builds jq queries for JSON field extraction, filtering, transformation, aggregation, and output formatting.
Builds yq queries for YAML and TOML files, including Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and GitHub Actions files.
Shows patterns for reading package.json, tsconfig, ESLint, Prettier, and other configuration files.
Helps convert TOML, YAML, and JSON views with yq input and output options.
Provides examples for arrays, objects, grouping, sorting, pivots, and multi-file processing.
Documents yq in-place edit patterns for controlled YAML updates.
limitations: Requires jq and yq to be installed in the execution environment.
Does not validate whether extracted data is correct for your business rules.
Commands only operate on files or responses available to the assistant or user.
In-place yq edits can modify files and should be reviewed before use.

use_cases.title: Inspect project configuration
use_cases.description: Extract dependencies, scripts, compiler options, and formatter settings from common project configuration files.

use_cases.title: Review deployment manifests
use_cases.description: Query service names, container images, labels, workflow jobs, and environment sections from infrastructure files.

use_cases.title: Filter structured exports
use_cases.description: Transform API responses and exported datasets into focused lists, counts, groups, and reports.

prompt_templates.title: Extract basic fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Use jq to show the project name, version, and available scripts from package.json. Explain the command in one sentence.

prompt_templates.title: Filter records by condition
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a jq command that lists active users from data.json with their id, name, and email fields only.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect deployment YAML
prompt_templates.prompt: Use yq to summarize service names, images, ports, and environment keys from docker-compose.yml without changing the file.

prompt_templates.title: Compare complex manifests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create jq or yq commands to compare two manifest files and summarize changed images, labels, ports, and resource names.

output_examples.input: Request: Summarize dependencies and scripts from package.json.
output: A grouped dependency summary for runtime and development packages.
A list of available project scripts with short purpose notes.

output_examples.input: Request: Review a Docker Compose file for service images and exposed ports.
output: A service table with image names, port mappings, and missing fields.
A short note about services that use similar images or unexpected ports.
The yq commands used for repeatable inspection.

output_examples.input: Request: Convert a TOML dependency section into a JSON-oriented view.
output_examples.output: The result is a readable dependency summary and a yq command that performs the conversion.

best_practices: Start with read-only queries before using commands that modify files.
Quote jq and yq filters consistently so shells do not alter them.
Review command output before using it in scripts or automation.
anti_patterns: Do not run in-place edits on important files without a backup or version control diff.
Do not paste secret values into sample JSON, YAML, or command prompts.
Do not assume a query is correct without checking representative input data.

faq.question: What file formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on JSON with jq and YAML or TOML with yq.

faq.question: Does it install jq or yq for me?
faq.answer: No. jq and yq must already be installed in the environment where commands run.

faq.question: Can it modify YAML files?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes yq in-place edit patterns, but file changes should be reviewed first.

faq.question: Can it process Kubernetes and Docker Compose files?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for images, services, labels, jobs, steps, and environment sections.

faq.question: Does it send data to external services?
faq.answer: No automatic network behavior is defined. One reference example shows a user-run curl query to the public GitHub API.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill in a repository?
faq.answer: Yes. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the required CLI tools are available.
